articles.title: 'It's a real shame': World No. 1 tennis doubles player takes aim at ATP bosses over trophy ceremony snub
articles.summary: World No. 1 doubles player Henry Patten criticised ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for missing the year-end doubles No.
articles.body: World No. 1 doubles player Henry Patten criticised ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for missing the year-end doubles No. 1 trophy presentation in Turin on Monday. Patten, who received the award alongside Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara, said it was disappointing that the two senior officials were not present for the ceremony.The pair collected their trophy from ATP chief tour officer Andre Silva. Patten and Heliovaara have won five titles this year, including Wimbledon."I never would have dreamt that we would be in the position that we're in now. For us it's a really big deal. It's a real shame that the ATP chairman and the ATP CEO don't think the same," Patten said."It would have been nice to have them on court with us today, but here we are by ourselves."Patten and Heliovaara have repeatedly questioned the ATP's approach to doubles, particularly its proposals to introduce smaller draws and reduce prize money from the 2028 season.Patten, along with Dutch player Sem Verbeek, led an open letter calling for the proposed reforms to be scrapped. The letter was signed by more than 100 players, including former doubles champions Bob and Mike Bryan.Heliovaara also addressed the crowd during the presentation, thanking Patten and the rest of their team for their contribution to the partnership."I'm going to say that Henry is the best partner in the world for doubles. I've been lucky enough to play with him for two and a half years."We shared a lot of wins, a lot of losses, but most of all, a lot of time everywhere in the world, really. On the court, off court, it's been a very nice, amazing trip together. But it's not just the two of us, I think it's also our team there in the box, in the spotlight today."I would like that we also give a big hand to every one of them. It's a lot of sacrifices from us, from the team, and obviously our families at home. Everybody who has helped us to achieve something like this. And to have a trophy like that at home, we will be very proud for a very long time."Patten and Heliovaara will now focus on their remaining matches at the ATP Finals in Turin. They began their round-robin campaign with a win on Sunday, defeating Orlando Luz and Rafael Matos in a match tie-break to move to 1-0.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Aryna Sabalenka's on-court meltdowns can no longer be ignored
articles.summary: Deep into her match against Elina Svitolina at Indian Wells Tennis Garden last week, Aryna Sabalenka erupted in a flurry of words.
articles.body: Deep into her match against Elina Svitolina at Indian Wells Tennis Garden last week, Aryna Sabalenka erupted in a flurry of words. Lip readers were quick to interpret her outburst, which came as she collected balls before serving in third set, as an attack on Ukrainians.Soon after the match, a clip began circulating on social media, with Sabalenka accused of saying, “those @#$ing Ukrainians” in Russian.Her voice, however, is inaudible in the footage, drowned out by the crowd noise and the chair umpire calling the score at 30-40.The 28-year-old later apologised on social media, clarifying that her comments were directed at a group of spectators who had been bothering her.“My comment was not directed at Elina,” Sabalenka said in a social media post. “I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.” Svitolina, responding to Sabalenka's explanation, pointed out that the support for her was hardly surprising.“There are many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match,” she said. The Ukrainian also recalled receiving unsavoury comments about the war during some of their previous encounters. “In some matches that we’ve played there have been not great comments towards me regards the war. It is like this in social media, sometimes things are turned around a little bit.”Sabalenka appeared to have put the disappointment of losing the Australian Open final to Elena Rybakina in Jan behind her, completing the Indian Wells-Miami double in March. But even amid that success, a pattern of emotional outbursts has become increasingly difficult to ignore.At the French Open quarterfinals in June, she suffered one of the most dramatic collapses of her career.Against Diana Shnaider, Sabalenka appeared to be cruising at 6-3, 5-3 before losing 10 consecutive games and going down 6-3, 5-7, 0-6. She screamed at her coaching team, struggled to rein in her frustration and unravelled as the match slipped away. At the post-match press conference, she described herself as having fallen into a “deep, dark hole”.Meltdowns are hardly uncommon in tennis, on either tour. The sport is unforgiving, leaving players alone with their frustrations, mistakes and the consequences of a match slipping away. But there is a distinction between venting anger at oneself, aracket or even one’s team, and directing it at an opponent or those supporting them. When a player of Sabalenka's stature finds herself embroiled in such episodes, the implications extend beyond the heat of the moment.At the 2025 French Open, where she reached the final, Sabalenka lost to Coco Gauff after taking the opening set, struggling to cope with the windy conditions. Her postmatch presser proved almost as revealing as the defeat itself. She described it as the worst tennis she had played in months before questioning how Gauff had managed to negotiate the conditions.“Honestly sometimes it felt like she was hitting the ball from the frame. Somehow magically the ball lands in the court, and you kind of, like, on the back foot. It felt like a joke,” she said. Ten days later, Sabalenka apologised to Gauff, admitting that her remarks had been “completely unprofessional”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Machac logra ante Draxl la primera victoria de la fase final de Bolonia
articles.standfirst: Lehecka clasificó a Chequia para las semifinales tras ganar a Aliassime
articles.summary: Lehecka clasificó a Chequia para las semifinales tras ganar a Aliassime
articles.body: la República Checa se ha anotado la primera victoria parcial de la fase final de la Copa Davis 2026, que se celebra en el Super Tennis Arena de Bolonia por segundo año consecutivo. Tomas Machac, el 59 del ranking ATP, ha logrado el primer punto para su país tras acabar con la resistencia del desconocido Liam Draxl, el 154 del mundo, por 6-2, 6-3 y 6-2. El triunfo de Machac dio después la opción a su compatriota Jiri Lehecka de lograr el billete a las semifinales. Su rival tenía más entidad que Draxl porque se tataba de Felix-Auger Aliassime, que viene de ser segundo reserva en las ATP Finals de Turín. El principal hándicap del canadiense es que no disputaba un partido oficial desde que se vio obligado a retirarse en los octavos del Masters 1000 de Shanghái con Caspe Ruud. Lo pagó caro, con una derrota por 7-6(4) y 6-2. El conjunto norteamericano tiene las sensibles bajas de Denis Shapovalov y Gabriel Diallo. Los checos, capitaneados por Tomas Berdych, esperan en la penúltima ronda al ganador de la serie que disputarán este miércoles la anfitriona Italia con Corea del Sur.

articles.title: Trinity Rodman, Ben Shelton Reportedly Split After Dating for Nearly 2 Years
articles.summary: Tennis star Ben Shelton and soccer star Trinity Rodman are reportedly no longer an item.
articles.body:
Tennis star Ben Shelton and soccer star Trinity Rodman are reportedly no longer an item.

According to Daniel Matthews of the Daily Mail , Shelton and Rodman have ended their relationship after nearly two years together.

Shelton and Rodman went public with their relationship in March 2025. They were frequently seen supporting each other at their respective matches.

Rodman was a staple in the spectator section as Shelton made a surprise run to the US Open final this past summer. The USWNT star, who also stars for the Washington Spirit in the NWSL, had a game earlier in the day but managed to make it from D.C. to New York to watch Shelton's final, where he lost to Alexander Zverev. Shelton was just as supportive when Rodman and the Spirit lost the 2025 NWSL championship match to Gotham FC last November.

According to Matthews, the two sports stars' "conflicting work schedules and constant travel made it too challenging for the couple to continue maintaining their relationship." However, they "are believed to remain close, despite their split."

Shelton had spoken about the hardships of their travel schedules and the impact on their relationship earlier this fall.

"It is really difficult," he told US Weekly in September, per Matthews. "I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time. ... None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways."

Rodman, who is recovering from a back injury, will focus on the USWNT's upcoming CONCACAF W Championship quarterfinal match against El Salvador on Friday.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner: World number two has 'minor' surgery on knee after lengthy injury absence
articles.summary: World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.
articles.body:
World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.

The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July.

In a post on Instagram, Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee.

"Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," the 25-year-old wrote.

"After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we'd all hoped.

"I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."

Earlier in November, Sinner said his goal was to go to Australia and potentially "play a few tournaments" before the first Grand Slam of the year begins on 17 January.

However, the Italian has also stressed the need to think of his long-term career in protecting his body.

The Instagram post is the first time Sinner has specified what the knee issue is.

In a video posted on his Youtube channel in October, Sinner said he had also lost "a lot of weight" after having his tonsils removed.

He also described having "days where I felt nothing and could play without any problems, and then days where I couldn't move at all".

He suffered a nasty fall in the first match of his Wimbledon title defence and also had blood seeping through his shoes because of a problematic toenail.

Alexander Zverev has become world number one in Sinner's absence, while rival Carlos Alcaraz swept four titles after returning from his injury lay-off in September.

Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches.

He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters' , and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way.

However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title.

Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece.

He ended his season in early October , meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025.

Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking.

Having met in three of the four Grand Slam finals last year, Sinner and Alcaraz played each other only once in 2026.

Sinner won their final at the Monte Carlo Masters shortly before Alcaraz spent four months out with a wrist injury.

Alcaraz's victory at the season-ending ATP Finals means he is only 350 ranking points behind Sinner - although the Spaniard will be defending 2,000 of those at the Australian Open.

"It's a shame we don't have Jannik," Alcaraz told SuperTennis TV , external after winning the ATP Finals on Sunday.

"We really miss him. I have not seen him for many months right now since I got injured in April.

"I can't wait to see him fit, healthy. I am pretty sure that he is going to come back even better and stronger."

Alcaraz will be the defending champion in Melbourne, having beaten Djokovic to complete a historic career Grand Slam in January.

articles.title: Alcaraz vuelve a los entrenos este miércoles en Bolonia y se aleja de los individuales ante Austria
articles.standfirst: El murciano está previsto que se ejercite dos horas en la pista 3, junto a Granollers y Pedro Martínez
articles.summary: El murciano está previsto que se ejercite dos horas en la pista 3, junto a Granollers y Pedro Martínez
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha descansado por segundo día este martes en Bolonia y será este miércoles cuando tenga la primera toma de contacto con la superficie de juego del Super Tennis Arena, según ha podido saber MARCA. La selección nacional tiene dos horas reservada la pista 3 y allí estará Alcaraz tres días después de coronarse maestro ATP en Turín. Sus acompañantes en la sesión serán Marcel Granollers y Pedro Martínez. La sesión se alargará dos horas, de las 11:00 horas a las 13. Rafa Jódar y Dani Mérida entrenarán juntos por segundo día seguido en la central porque, en un principio, serán ellos los que disputen los individuales del jueves. Carlitos está haciendo un esfuerzo titánico por ayudar al equipo a la consecución de la séptima Ensaladera de plata. Cabe recordar que terminó su participación en el Masters masculino con un estabilizador rotuliano em su rodilla derecha y una muslera y un vendaje en la izquierda. Alcaraz podría sería reservado en los individuales del jueves con Austria (esa es la idea inicial) y sólo jugaría el dobles en caso de que sea necesario y el marcador sea de 1-1. Formaría pareja con Marcel Granollers. No jugar contra el conjunto austriaco significaría ganar dos días más de descanso y de recuperación con vistas a la semifinal del sábado con el ganador de la serie entre Alemania y Gran Bretaña. El campeón de siete grandes, para preservar al máximo su físico, programó tres entrenos exprés sus últimos tres días de competición en Turín 40 minutos antes de saltar a la pista. Alcaraz se encontrará una superficie de juego de la empresa española GreenSet, liderada por Javier Sánchez Vicario y la misma que levantó la instalación del Inalpi Arena de Turín. El cambio más sensible son las pelotas, de Dunlop a Yonex Platinum. Las mismas que se encontró el tenista en la gira asiática, en los torneos de Tokio y el Masters 1000 de Shanghái.

articles.title: Un deporte de cuerpos rotos
articles.standfirst: Carlos Alcaraz fue un coloso en las ATP Finals de Turín. Se llevó el título, a pesar de los dolores. El calendario del deporte mundial está plagado de partes médicos
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz fue un coloso en las ATP Finals de Turín. Se llevó el título, a pesar de los dolores. El calendario del deporte mundial está plagado de partes médicos
articles.body: El fin de semana enseñó de nuevo el músculo del deporte español, pero también mostró la realidad que ilustra el calendario de competiciones: los deportistas llegan a final de año hechos unos harapos. Carlos Alcaraz, que llevaba cinco meses lesionado, alzó el título de maestros entre resonancias, frente a Alexander Zverev, que también tenía problemas en el pie al sacar. Marc Márquez, antes, había conquistado un Mundial que ha ganado con brazo y medio. En el derecho lleva arrastrando las consecuencias de la lesión sufrida en el GP de Indonesia de 2025. Ya en esta temporada fue operado del pie y del hombro derecho tras caerse en Le Mans. Que haya ganado el título con un cuerpo así es una proeza. El parte médico 2026 del tenis es terrorífico. El actual top 10 mundial sólo ha coincidido en un torneo: Indian Wells. Entre Jannick Sinner, cuyo futuro aún no está despejado y no llegará ni a Australia; Alcaraz y Fils suman más de 12 meses fuera de las pistas. Sólo tres jugadores: Zverev, Medvedev y Paul han superado los 70 partidos en este curso, la mitad de tenistas que el año pasado. Es la cifra más baja desde la pandemia. El panorama es igual de sombrío en el fútbol, golpeado en las últimas temporadas por un torrente de roturas de cruzados. A más competiciones, formatos ampliados y selecciones que se suman al calendario de los clubes, el propio juego es una trampa. El fútbol actual tiene más sprints, más frenadas y más cambios de dirección a alta velocidad que hace 10 años. Esos gestos de desaceleración son mortales. El giro con la rodilla casi extendida son el mecanismo típico de la rotura, casi siempre sin contacto. El deporte, lógicamente, puede estar sujeto a inconvenientes. Se ha visto en el ciclismo y en el skate, con las clavículas rotas de Pogacar y Bijueska, el esloveno más tres vértebras. Eso entra dentro de los accidentes. Pero todo lo anterior relatado no forma parte de este grupo. Responde a la necesidad de poblar el calendario de competición. Patrocinadores y televisiones exigen presencia constante. Los deportistas, por compromiso o por miedo a perder su sitio, vuelven antes de tiempo. Adiós a aquello de diagnóstico conservador. Ojalá el próximo titular no sea cuánto sufrió el campeón, sino qué bien pudo competir.

articles.title: Feliciano López, director de la Copa Davis: "Es un regalo tener a Alcaraz y Zverev"
articles.standfirst: El toledano cumple su cuarto año como cabeza visible de la Final a 8 de la máxima competición por países
articles.summary: El toledano cumple su cuarto año como cabeza visible de la Final a 8 de la máxima competición por países
articles.body: Feliciano López, a sus 45 años, suma su cuarto como director de las Finales de la Copa Davis. El toledano se sienta con MARCA en el Super Tennis Arena de la capital de la región Emilia Romaña para hablar del torneo y la presencia de Carlos Alcaraz y Alexander Zverev. Pregunta. ¿Cómo se presentan estas finales? Respuesta. Estamos contentos. Después de una época en la que ha habido muchos cambios, que han confundido un poco a la gente, al aficionado, al jugador, las nuevas generaciones empiezan a entender lo que significa la Copa Davis. Se ha hablado con federaciones, capitanes, jugadores, para llegar donde hemos llegado ahora. La esencia del torneo se ha recuperado, con dos eliminatorias al año con el formato antiguo. Creo que eso era muy importante. Eso permite que muchos chicos jóvenes, que no han tenido la oportunidad de vivir la Copa Davis en directo, porque les ha cogido en los años que era un formato distinto, tienen la oportunidad de vivir la experiencia. Si no lo has vivido no puedes tener una opinión. La atmósfera de jugar en casa... P. Usted estuvo en Málaga recibiendo en el aeropuerto a Djokovic y a Sinner. Estuvo el lunes en el hotel con Alcaraz. ¿Les ve la ilusión de ganar? R. Yo sí lo veo. En Djokovic lo he visto como jugador cuando jugamos contra Serbia. Con Sinner y Djokovic lo vi en Málaga después de matarse entre ellos después de Turín. Eso es lo que queremos recuperar. Y me parece el mejor ejemplo del mundo ver a Novak, el mejor de la historia con los números en la mano, estar la última semana del año representando a Serbia, intentando ganar la Ensaladera, fue la consolidación del actual formato. Necesitas a los mejores para tener el ejemplo claro de que hay que hacer el esfuerzo. Que estuvieran Djokovic y Sinner fue un punto de inflexión. y ahora tienes a Carlos aquí, que acaba de ganar el Masters, que ha estado cuatro meses parado... Y está aquí para ayudar a España a ganar. Sinner estaría aquí hoy sino hubiera estado lesionado. Su compromiso con Italia es brutal. P. ¿Necesitaban que Alcaraz estuviera? R. Es lógico, queremos a todos como en cualquier torneo. A Rafa le encantaba jugar la Copa Davis; que le pregunten a Federer qué sintió cuando ganó. Lo que queremos es que los jugadores jóvenes entiendan qué significa. Tener a Carlos aquí es un regalo; tener a Zverev, número 1, es otro regalo. Es una pena que jugándose en Italia no esté Sinner. Espero que vuelva cuanto antes. P. Como director es imparcial, ¿pero tiene su corazoncito? R. Yo soy español y me encanta que gane España. Cuando están jugando los partidos hay momentos de tensión donde tu corazón tira para un lado. Pero yo no soy cualquier fan que está en la grada. Soy el director. Si me pregunta si me gustaría que España ganara la Copa Davis, pues evidentemente. El año pasado, cuando perdió España con Italia, estaba triste por los chicos, por su esfuerzo. Por otro lado también me dije: ‘qué mérito Italia, ganar en tu país’. Cuando trabajas en el otro lado de la industria pierdes un poco ese sentimiento. Como director de Madrid hay jugadores y jugadoras que tengo un vínculo más cercano y me hace más ilusión que ganen. Pero eso es aparte del trabajo, soy neutral. P. ¿Es el año de España? R. Tienen al que para mí es el mejor jugador del mundo. Un segundo tenista que es top10, que es Rafa Jódar. Davidovich que no ha podido venir. Y luego tenemos a Pedro, que es un gran jugador de Copa Davis porque responde muy bien. Incluso sube su nivel. Marcel es el mejor doblista de la actualidad. Es que ha jugado Copa Daviis conmigo, con Marc López, con Rafa, con Pedro, con Carlos, y con todos ha jugado bien. No hay que tener miedo a decir que España es favorita. Junto a Italia son las favoritas. Ojo con Alemania. Es verdad que en este formato de tres partidos a tres sets todo se iguala mucho. El dobles es un 33 por ciento. En los países con tantos buenos jugadores si hubiera cuatro individuales su margen sería muy grande. P. A Carlitos sólo le falta la Copa Davis y el oro olímpico. R. Yo nunca he hablado con él de esto, pero seguro que la ilusión que tiene por ganar es enorme. En la historia del tenis tener la Copa Davis en tu palmarés es algo relevante y todos los grandes de la historia la tienen. Es una experiencia diferente compartir aquí con tus compañeros, se disfruta de una manera distinta. P. ¿Se entiende mejor la relevancia de esta competición cuando se gana? R. Puede ser que sí, pero creo que la entiendes más cuando vives una emoción grande en una eliminatoria relativamente importante. Si además es una final y ganas hay un reconocimiento muy grande en tu país, la gente se identifica contigo, se sienten orgullosos de lo que has hecho. Pero lo que engancha es la experiencia de competir en Copa Davis. Yo no había vivido una experiencia en el torneo y me tocó debutar en una final, en Australia y en hierba. Llegas ahí, ves eso lleno, los himnos, los aficionados en España viendo los partidos a las tres de la mañana... En el circuito juegas para ti. Aquí puedes hacer feliz a mucha gente y es una responsabilidad muy grande a la vez que bonita. P. El mayor éxtasis que vivió usted fue en Mar del Plata? R. Sí, sin duda. Jugar una eliminatoria de Copa Davis no hay color con jugar en otro lado. La manera cómo entiende la gente el deporte cuando la selección está implicada es increíble. Nunca vamos a poder vivir las emociones que se vivieron en ese pabellón. La gente cantando cuatro o cinco horas sin parar, jugar contra Delpo, el dobles, es una experiencia que me llevo para siempre.

articles.title: Juanjo Moreno hace el trabajo con Alcaraz y regresa este jueves a España
articles.standfirst: El fisioterapeuta y preparador físico ha acompañado a Carlitos en sus tres primeros días en Bolonia
articles.summary: El fisioterapeuta y preparador físico ha acompañado a Carlitos en sus tres primeros días en Bolonia
articles.body: La imagen de Juanjo Moreno es siempre reconocible al lado de Carlos Alcaraz. "Tengo al mejor fisio del mundo", reconocía Carlitos hace un año cuando este obró el milagro y le recuperó del tobillo para ganar el título de Tokio. Juanjo es la sombra del campeón de siete grandes desde hace ocho años y vive pendiente de todos los detalles. Por eso le ha acompañado los tres primeros días en Bolonia para seguir con el tratamiento y la recuperación del cuerpo de un Carlitos que salió de las ATP Finals de Turín con un estabilizador rotuliano en la rodilla derecha y un vendaje y una muslera en la pierna izquierda. Moreno vuelve este jueves a casa con los deberes hechos. Parte de la culpa del éxito del Alcaraz pasa por sus manos y sus conocimientos. Desde los análisis de sangre del tenista (en los que se observó que es mejor la comida sin gluten) hasta su condición de cruzado para el tenis porque su mano es la derecha y su ojo principal el izquierdo. Licenciado en Ciencias de la Actividad Física del Deporte y posteriormente en Fisioterapia, fue también el que buscó el jugo de pepinillo para combatir los calambres que sintió su jugador durante las semifinales de Roland Garros 2023 con Novak Djokovic. Juanjo empezó a trabajar con el cuerpo de Carlitos en 2018, coincidiendo con el fichaje de Juan Carlos Ferrero como entrenador. Cambió el equipo de fútbol del Yeclano por la Academia de Ferrero de Villena. Sus primeras experiencias profesionales habían sido en Francia, primero en Lyon, luego en Marsella y posteriormente en París. Alcaraz siempre sale enchufado a la pista tras un calentamiento que tiene una parte de fuerza, explosividad, coordinación, habilidad oculo manual (juegos malabares), además de hacer hincapié en los tendones. Alcaraz se queda en Bolonia junto a su entrenador Samuel López, que hizo el viaje con él desde Turín el lunes en coche.

articles.title: Arthur Rinderknech denies refusing doping test after L'Equipe report
articles.summary: French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.
articles.body:
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) confirmed the world number 57 is under investigation, after a report by L'Equipe , external earlier on Wednesday.

It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector".

Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision.

Rinderknech issued a statement on Instagram in response to L'Equipe's report, saying: "I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation and I have already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal, as is my right."

The 31-year-old, who beat current world number one Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, believes he will then be "exonerated of the test refusal allegation".

"I have never taken any banned substance and I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always," he added.

The ITIA said the case would be heard by a tribunal early next year and expressed regret that the investigation was first reported by a media outlet.

"We go to great lengths to keep cases confidential, and we are disappointed that the details have become public in this way," an ITIA statement added.

articles.summary: Rafa Jódar y Dani Mérida jugarán los dos primeros puntos de la serie con Austria
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha empezado a entrenar este miércoles en la pista 2 del Super Tennis Arena de Bolonia para prepararse para la fase final de la Copa Davis. Como adelantó MARCA el lunes, Alcaraz estará para el dobles contra Austria, en caso de que sea necesario y la serie vaya 1-1, pero será reservado en los individuales, que jugarán Rafa Jódar y Dani Mérida. Los dos jóvenes madrileños serán los que se midan en los dos primeros puntos a Jurij Rodionov y Lukas Neumayer. El seleccionador nacional, David Ferrer, supervisó toda su práctica en la central mientras Marc López, su segundo, se quedaba para entrenar por parejas. Alcaraz necesita más descanso y, en caso de ganar 2-0 al conjunto austriaco, tendría dos más de tratamiento y recuperación para estar listo de cara a las semifinales con Alemania o Gran Bretaña. El jueves habrán pasado 736 días desde que el nuevo maestro de la ATP jugó un partido de dobles en competición oficial. Fue el de los cuartos de la Copa Davis 2024, con derrota ante los neerlandeses Wesley Koolhof y Botic van de Zandschulp en la fase final del Martín Carpena de Málaga. Desde entonces, sus tres únicas apariciones a mitad de pista han sido en la Laver Cup. En la de San Francisco, en 2025, junto a Jakub Mensik, derrotaron a los americanos Taylor Fritz y Alex Michelsen. Con Casper Ruud se impusieron a Michelsen y Reilly Opelka. En 2026 formó otra vez dúo con Mensik para derrotar a Alexander Bublik y Fritz. La estrategia ideada por la selección nacional es que Carlitos salte a jugar el dobles al lado de Granollers siempre que las eliminatorias vayan 1-1.

articles.title: Rinderknech se arriesga a una sanción por rechazar un control antidopaje
articles.standfirst: Su caso será estudiado por la ITIA el próximo mes de febrero
articles.summary: Su caso será estudiado por la ITIA el próximo mes de febrero
articles.body: El tenista francés Arthur Rinderknech, actual 57 ATP y que llegó a alcanzar el 24 como mejor ranking el pasado mes de mayo, se arriesga a una suspensión de cuatro años por rechazar someterse a un control antidopaje por sorpresa el pasado mes de junio. Según informa L'Equipe, el tenista es objeto de un proceso por parte de la ITIA, la Agencia Internacional para la Integridad en el Tenis. Según la secuencia del hecho, el pasado mes de junio el tenista recibió la visita de un agente antidopaje, de habla inglesa. Arthir alegó tener prisa para coger un tren y firmó un documento de negativa sin apercibirse de las consecuencias. Una negativa a un control no implica suspensión automática, de modo que Rinderknech ha estado jugando hasta el pasado Masters 1.000 de París. El tenista será objeto de una audiencia de la ITIA el próximo mes de febrero. El tenista ha emitido un comunicado a través de sus redes sociales en el que señala su extrañeza por la difusión del caso -"creía que el proceso era estrictamente confidencial"- y señala que quiere que el asunto sea visto por un tribunal independiente, estando entonces seguro que será absuelto. "Nunca he tomado ninguna sustancia prohibida y estoy orgulloso de mi comportamiento y como compromiso con el tenis", concluye.

articles.title: Arthur Rinderknech denies refusing to take anti-doping test after charge confirmed for French tennis player
articles.summary: French newspaper L'Equipe reported Arthur Rinderknech's alleged refusal to take doping test; International ‌Tennis Integrity Agency has since confirmed charge; former ⁠Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova handed four-year ban in June after tribunal found she refused test
articles.body:
The International ‌Tennis Integrity Agency [ITIA] confirmed on Wednesday that the 31-year-old had been charged for refusing a test in Brittany in June after French newspaper L'Equipe initially reported in their story that he was facing a four-year ban.

Rinderknech denied the allegation on Instagram, while stressing that he has never taken a banned substance and revealing he has asked for the ​matter to be heard by an independent tribunal.

The ITIA said in a statement: "Following media reports and the player's social media post, we can confirm that Arthur Rinderknech has been charged with refusing a test.

"We go to great lengths to keep cases confidential, and we are disappointed that the details have become public in this way.

"The case will be heard by an independent tribunal early next year and we will not be commenting further on the specifics of the investigation."

The ITIA also explained that the maximum length ban Rinderknech could face if found to have refused a test is four years, but could be up to two years if the panel determines there is no significant fault.

Rinderknech: I have ​never taken any banned substance

Rinderknech had earlier written: "I am aware of the reports regarding my alleged test refusal case ​with the ITIA which according to the ITIA, was ⁠supposed to be kept strictly confidential.

"I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation, and I have ‌already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal as is my right.

"It is my belief that when the matter is presented to the independent tribunal I will be ⁠exonerated of the test refusal allegation.

"I have ​never taken any banned substance and I am ​proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which ​have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always."

Former ⁠Wimbledon women's champion Marketa Vondrousova received a four-year ban in June after an independent tribunal found she refused an anti-doping test in December ⁠2025, with the Czech since appealing to the Court ​of Arbitration for Sport.

Rinderknech has a highest career ranking of 24 and reached the final of the Shanghai Masters 1000 event in 2025 before losing in straight sets to cousin ‌Valentin Vacherot of Monaco.

Rinderknech's best Grand Slam result is reaching the fourth round of the US Open last year, while he beat current world No 1 Alexander Zverev in the first round of Wimbledon in 2025.

articles.title: Sinner uncertain for Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery
articles.summary: The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played a match since winning Wimbledon in July.
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner risks missing the Australian Open in January after confirming that he has undergone surgery on his troublesome right knee .

The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played a match since winning Wimbledon for the second time in July, with less than two months until the start of the first major tournament of the season in Melbourne.

“Over the past few months, together with my team we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery,” Sinner said in a statement on Tuesday.

“After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.”

The procedure, which had been reported earlier in the day by broadcasters RAI and Sky Sport, and sports daily La Gazzetta dello Sport, was performed by knee injury specialist Lasse Lempainen at a clinic in Finland.

Another knee specialist, Fabrizio Terrone at the Isokinetic centre in Turin, told Sky Sport that Sinner’s absence could last “at least three to four months”.

That means the earliest Sinner might be back on court with a racket in hand would be during the American hard-court swing, at Indian Wells and Miami Masters.

The 25-year-old admitted recently that the worst injury of his career left him barely able to move.

“The worst part for me about this injury is that I cannot compete, I cannot play tennis,” said Sinner in a recent video.

“Also, my life outside of tennis is a bit more limited because of a simple fact that I cannot do things that I really like, because I want to protect my knee.”

Sinner, a two-time champion at the Australian Open which begins on January 17, recently said that he will make his comeback at the “Six Kings Slam” tournament in Saudi Arabia, which has been rescheduled for late December due to the conflict with Yemen’s Houthis.

But that now looks impossible and a difficult start to 2027 seems in store for the man who has in recent years risen to be, alongside Spanish star Carlos Alcaraz, the pre-eminent force in men’s tennis.

Sinner was having a brilliant campaign before being stopped by his knee problem, with five Masters 1000 titles going alongside his triumph at Wimbledon.

The Italian’s 94 percent winning record in 2026 is the best of his career, even beating his figures from the previous two seasons in each of which he won two Grand Slams and the ATP Finals.

He suffered a major disappointment at the French Open when, leading Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo by two sets and 5-1 ahead in the third, he succumbed to heatstroke and was eliminated in the second round.

Sinner recently lost top spot in the men’s world rankings to losing Wimbledon finalist Alexander Zverev, who has taken advantage of injury problems for both Sinner and Alcaraz to win Roland Garros and the US Open.

articles.title: La Rafa Nadal Academy reunirá a las leyendas del tenis español en su décimo aniversario
articles.standfirst: David Ferrer, Albert Costa, Feliciano López, Carla Suárez, Anabel Medina, Sergi Bruguera, Roberto Bautista y Nicolás Almagro, además del propio Rafa Nadal, han confirmado ya su presencia
articles.summary: David Ferrer, Albert Costa, Feliciano López, Carla Suárez, Anabel Medina, Sergi Bruguera, Roberto Bautista y Nicolás Almagro, además del propio Rafa Nadal, han confirmado ya su presencia
articles.body: La Rafa Nadal Academy reunirá el próximo 12 de diciembre a destacadas figuras del tenis en un evento que permitirá compartir los primeros diez años de la academia con algunos de los protagonistas de la historia del tenis español en las instalaciones de la academia en Manacor (Mallorca). Según anunció este miércoles la academia, este evento, denominado 'El Gran Encuentro del Tenis Español', se enmarca en los actos de conmemoración de su décimo aniversario. Veintiocho tenistas han confirmado su presencia en la isla para dicha celebración, entre los que destacan nombres como David Ferrer, Albert Costa, Feliciano López, Carla Suárez, Anabel Medina, Sergi Bruguera, Roberto Bautista o Nicolás Almagro, además del propio Rafa Nadal. Los asistentes tendrán la oportunidad de volver a disfrutar en pista de algunas de las grandes figuras de diferentes generaciones, que compartirán protagonismo en un dinámico torneo de dobles por equipos. El 'Gran Encuentro del Tenis Español' ofrecerá una ocasión para reconocer la contribución de sus protagonistas al crecimiento y consolidación de este deporte y compartir el significado de una celebración que conecta con la esencia de la academia, transmitir a las nuevas generaciones la experiencia y los valores de quienes han abierto camino en el tenis español. La cita dará continuidad a los actos conmemorativos del décimo aniversario, que vivieron uno de sus momentos más especiales el pasado 3 de octubre con el Rafa Nadal Academy Slam.

articles.title: Alcaraz y la operación de Sinner: "El tenis y yo le echamos de menos, no le veo desde abril"
articles.standfirst: El murciano valoró la lesión de rodilla del italiano, que le ha obligado a pasar por el quirófano
articles.summary: El murciano valoró la lesión de rodilla del italiano, que le ha obligado a pasar por el quirófano
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y el resto de la selección nacional de la Copa Davis ha realizado este miércoles su primera rueda de prensa antes de su debut mañana en la serie de cuartos de la máxima competición por países contra Austria. Alcaraz valoró la lesión y la operación de Janni Sinner. "El tenis y yo le echamos de menos. No le veo desde abril. Va a volver más fuerte. Le deseo una recuperación lo más rápido posible". El murciano se refiere a la final del Masters 1000 de Montecarlo, que cayó del lado del italiano. El maestro de las ATP Finals avisa de que "estoy cuidando los problemas físicos que tuve en Turín. Espero no tener problemas en los próximos días. No han pasado muchos días, pero me encuentro bien. Hoy he tocado la pelota, no ha sido lo exigente que suele ser un entrenamiento previo a la competición. Tengo confianza plena juegue quien juegue". Alcaraz habló también de la mejoría en el servicio: "Quien pegue más fuerte a las líneas es el que gana. No suelo mirar las estadísticas en los entrenamientos. Pero sabemos la importancia que tiene el saque. Desde el US Open es la vez que más empeño le he puesto en el saque. Y la precisión era algo importante y lo hemos trabajado más porque no soy tan alto como otros". David Ferrer comentaba que "es una buena oportunidad para ganar. Pero ahora hay que pensar sólo en Austria. Paso a paso". Por su parte, Dani Mérida habla de su partido que abre la serie con Austria. "David tomará la mejor decisión. Yo afrontaré el partido como una semana más y que me sirva la experiencia de Chile si juego".

articles.title: Zverev Says He's 'Not Too Concerned' Over Lawsuit From Ex-Partner in Alleged Abuse Case
articles.summary: BOLOGNA, Italy (AP) — Top-ranked tennis player Alexander Zverev said he was "not too concerned" over a lawsuit filed by his former partner and re-asserted his innocence Wednesday in the alleged abuse case.
articles.body:
BOLOGNA, Italy (AP) — Top-ranked tennis player Alexander Zverev said he was "not too concerned" over a lawsuit filed by his former partner and re-asserted his innocence Wednesday in the alleged abuse case.

The mother of the former couple's daughter alleges Zverev violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports daily L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven."

Zverev was asked about the latest accusation while representing Germany at the Davis Cup Final 8.

"It's not a court case. What is it called? It's not a lawsuit. It's a statement that I'm supposed to have made. In my opinion, I didn't," he replied. "To be honest, I'm not really into it that much right now, so I don't really know too much about it. But, no, I'm not too concerned about it, to be honest."

Zverev was asked if he was misquoted by L'Equipe.

"I think I'm innocent. I've spoken about it enough," he said. "I'm really done talking about that subject because it's been, what, five years ago? Six years ago? So I've spoken enough about it."

Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, said in a statement last week that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit," Zverev's lawyers said. "If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion" protected by the German constitution.

They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, said Zverev's claim over his innocence "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client."

He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honor had been violated.

"Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form," he said. "Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement."

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and he be fined up to 250,000 euros ($275,000) every time if he does.

Zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to Patea during an argument in Berlin in May 2020. He always denied any wrongdoing.

The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement. Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organizations.

Zverev this month ascended to the No. 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two Grand Slam titles this year. He was beaten by Carlos Alcaraz in the championship match of the ATP Finals on Sunday.

Germany faces Britain in the Davis Cup quarterfinals on Thursday.

Zverev previously denied abuse allegations from another former girlfriend, Olga Sharypova, who first made the accusations in 2020.

The allegations prompted the men's professional tennis tour, the ATP, to investigate her claims. It ended 15 months later, in January 2023, with the ATP saying there was "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

articles.title: Davis Cup Finals: GB's Henry Patten on ending Harri Heliovaara partnership
articles.summary: Britain's Henry Patten agrees he was "ruthless" in splitting with doubles partner and close friend Harri Heliovaara, just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy.
articles.body:
Britain's Henry Patten agrees he was "ruthless" in splitting with his doubles partner and close friend Harri Heliovaara, just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy.

Heliovaara and Patten joined forces in 2024 and won Wimbledon together for the second time in July.

In a post on his blog, the Finnish player detailed the disappointment, shock and anger he felt when Patten phoned him with the news.

"I got a lot of stick for calling Harri to tell him," Patten told BBC Sport before Great Britain's Davis Cup quarter-final against Germany.

"I was crumpled over the toilet after the match and Harri, as he often does, had left very quickly to catch a flight back to his family.

"It was ruthless - it was a really difficult decision for me to make for two reasons.

"The first one is we are year-end number ones and we have a great track record together.

"Secondly, me and Harri grew really close during that time. I still consider Harri one of, if not my best friend.

"He's invited to my wedding in the summer. It was probably the first time in my career that I have had to make a decision like that, and I didn't enjoy it."

Patten's new partner will be compatriot Neal Skupski, who says he decided in the space of a "very stressful few hours" to end his pairing with American Christian Harrison.

Davis Cup Finals: Great Britain v Germany

Patten and Skupski could play their first match as a regular pair against Kevin Krawietz and Tim Putz to decide Britain's quarter-final against Germany on Thursday.

There is little doubt the dust is still settling on a bruising weekend.

"It was a very uncomfortable few hours, but we did speak over the phone for a long time,” Patten continued.

"Obviously I wasn't expecting him to be over the moon about it, and he absolutely has every right to be angry.

"But in that discussion I said I feel like this decision is based on the tennis. I feel that for both of us [it] has stagnated a bit.

"With some time, we'll still remain good friends. That's certainly my hope."

Patten says he has looked up to Skupski for a long time, and enjoys the energy he brings to the court.

He made contact with Ken Skupski, who coaches his brother, last Friday, and did not speak to Neal until he and Harrison had lost in the last four of the ATP Finals the following day.

"It was a very stressful few hours," Skupski recalled.

"After coming off the court, I went to lunch, spoke to [British doubles coach] Louis Cayer, who couldn't really tell me too much as other [British] players are involved.

"It was down to me and my brother to decide what I wanted to do and, at the end of the day, there was only one decision.

"That was the most difficult part - speaking to Christian. We spoke at the hotel, I told him that this opportunity doesn't come along very often to play with another Briton who is a world number one and be able to play Davis Cup and the Olympics in the future.

"So, I think he understood. I don't know if he quite believed me that we hadn't spoken beforehand, but it was two or three hours after the match in which I decided.

"I'm very happy and comfortable with my decision."

The singles in Bologna are likely to feature Arthur Fery and Cameron Norrie and, as British number one, Fery can expect one of the toughest tasks in men's tennis.

The 24-year-old will be up against world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion Alexander Zverev in the second singles match.

Zverev beat Fery in the Wimbledon semi-finals and again at the Vienna Open, with the Briton only winning two games the second time around.

"I've played him a few times already this year, so it's not going to be a completely new thing, which will help me," Fery told BBC Sport earlier in November.

"The serve for me is a challenge because he's close to 2m and I'm on the shorter side of the players out there.

"I struggled to return him, the ball just gets up a lot on me, but I have been working in practice to fight that.

"That's going to serve me not only against Zverev but in general."

Norrie is expected to face Jan-Lennard Struff in the first singles.

The German reached the quarter-finals of Wimbledon and, at 39 in the world, is currently 13 places above Norrie.

Norrie needs little motivation, but the fact Leon Smith is in his last week as captain after over 16 years in the role may help a little.

“I'm so grateful to be here and I think it adds a little bit of motivation to have Leon in our corner. I want to leave it all out there for him,” Norrie added.

“I really like playing with him on the bench there, I feel very relaxed, very chill, he knows when is the right moment to say something.

"He's a great leader and it's a great honour to be in his team."

articles.title: Berrettini y Vavassori salen al rescate de la campeona Italia ante Corea del Sur
articles.standfirst: Flavio Cobolli, el héroe en la pasada edición, perdió su partido con el coreano Kwon
articles.summary: Flavio Cobolli, el héroe en la pasada edición, perdió su partido con el coreano Kwon
articles.body: Italia, vigente campeona de la Copa Davis —han ganado las tres últimas ediciones, dos en Málaga y una en Bolonia—, vive una auténtica crisis interna en su vestuario que ha estado a punto de costarle la eliminación este miércoles en los cuartos con Corea del Sur. Tuvieron que ser Matteo Berrettini y Andrea Vavassori quienes dieran el pase a las semifinales en el decisivo punto del dobles tras la sorprendente derrota de Flavio Cobolli ante Soonwoo Kwon, por 3-6 y 7-6(3) y 7-6(5). El dúo italiano se impuso a Hyeon Chung y Kwon, por 7-6(2) y 7-6(11). Es la quinta semifinal consecutiva para ellos. Filippo Volandri, seleccionador transalpino, hizo una primera convocatoria para las finales en la que no estaba Berrettini por su distanciamiento con Lorenzo Musetti. Volandri se cargaba de entrada a un Matteo que es el tenista más carismático de la escuadra y cuyos resultados en la máxima competición por países están fuera de toda duda. Ha decantado a su favor sus últimos diez partidos , entre 2024 y 2026. Por eso el capitán local no dudo en repescarlo cuando presenció la semana pasada en directo en Turín el otro incendio en su vestuario entre su pareja de dobles: Simone Bolelli y Vavassori. Ambos decidieron terminar su relación profesional en la pasada gira asiática, pero tuvieron que jugar las ATP Finals porque estaban clasificados. Sin ningún tipo de química entre ambos perdieron sus tres partidos de la fase de grupos. Cobolli, el único top10’ en el equipo italiano y héroe de la última Ensaladera para su país en ausencia de Jannik Sinner, pide unidad para repetir victoria. “Necesitamos estar unidos”, afirma Cobolli, que mantiene una gran relación con Berrettini. De hecho, Matteo fue a verle los partidos en su debut la semana pasada en el Masters masculino reservado a los ocho mejores de la campaña. Los anfitriones llenaron la central del Super Tennis Arena de Bolonia para derrotar a Corea del Sur sudando la gota gorda. Musetti acabó con la resistencia de Seongchan Hong, por 6-0 y 7-6(5), pero el posterior traspié de Flavio lo complicó todo. Los transalpinos se medirán en las semifinales del viernes a una siempre peligrosa Chequia, que lleva dos años eliminando a Estados Unidos en los playoffs clasificatorios para las finales.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz's serve may be a work in progress, but the Spaniard is going places
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has played six tournaments since returning to competition in August and won four of them, taking his title tally for the year to six.
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz has played six tournaments since returning to competition in August and won four of them, taking his title tally for the year to six. But it is not just the number of titles, or even the fact that his last three triumphs have come on speedy indoor hardcourts - traditionally not the strongest part of his game - that makes this run particularly impressive. It is that he has achieved all this while his serve remains awork in progress.The 23-year-old Spaniard defeated world No. 1 Alexander Zverev in straight sets in Sunday’s title match in Turin to claim his first ATP Finals crown. Yet his average first-serve speed was nearly 8 kmph slower than what he had managed in last year’s final against Jannik Sinner.Alcaraz averaged 196 kmph on his first serve and 170 kmph on his second in Turin, although his second-serve speed against Zverev was significantly slower.Alcaraz, who injured his wrist in Barcelona in April, returned to competition at the US Open in August, where he reached the quarterfinals. Since then, he has won titles in Tokyo, Vienna, Paris and Turin, compiling an impressive 22-1 record in that stretch.After Sunday’s final, Alcaraz spoke about his grandfather, who reminds him of the three C’s before he steps on court, whether for a match or practice.“In Spanish it is ‘Cabeza, corazon, cajones’, in English it is ‘head, heart, balls’,” he said in Turin.While Alcaraz wasted little time rediscovering his forehand after returning to competition, the serve has proved adifferent challenge. The seven-time major champion, who stands at 6ft and, along with Italian Flavio Cobolli, is the shortest player in the ATP’s Top 10, has had to find ways to extract more from his serving action.There has been a subtle change in his motion since August, including a lift of the front foot that places more weight on the back foot and helps with the loading. He has also lowered his ball toss and quickened his motion. In the superfast indoor conditions in Turin, those adjustments gave his serve an added edge.“I understand how I should serve, and when I’m relaxed, I do a really smooth movement and I accelerate. When I feel nervous, I want to do more than I should do,” he said. “I’m not (a) server. I need to gain the point from the baseline, so I have to realise that and understand that. Once I got it, I think the serve goes much better.”Zverev may have finished the year as No. 1, but it is Alcaraz who has given the closing months of the season their most compelling storyline.He began 2026 under a barrage of questions after parting ways with Juan Carlos Ferrero, the coach who had guided him through his formative years, at the end of a successful 2025 season. The debate over whether the coach made the champion or the genius made the coach has, in many ways, been answered.Alcaraz has had to fight for his own territory this season, and his response has been emphatic. Ferrero has since signed up to work with 24-year-old world No. 4 Ben Shelton, who dismantled Alcaraz’s challenge at the US Open but has since lost twice to the Spaniard. Their meetings are already being talked up as one of the rivalries to watch in the new season.For Alcaraz, though, the bigger challenge will be to build on a remarkable finish to 2026. The serve is evolving, but he has shown that he can win on the biggest stages even when one of the most important weapons in his arsenal is not firing at full strength.If he can combine the improvements in his serve with the fluency of his baseline game, the prospect of an even more formidable Alcaraz in 2027 should concern the rest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery. The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July an...
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery.

The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first Grand Slam tournament of 2027.

Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery.

"Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028."

The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee.

Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: "Over the past few months, together with my team, we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery.

"After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we had all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.

"I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."

The Italian, who won the season-opening Grand Slam in 2024 and 2025, announced this week that he had gone under the knife at a clinic in Finland.

“Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028.

“We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon.”

Experts have speculated that Sinner’s absence could last three months.

That means the earliest he might be back in action would be during the American hard-court swing, at Indian Wells and the Miami Masters in February-March.

The 25-year-old Sinner was having a brilliant campaign before being stopped by his knee problem , with five Masters 1000 titles alongside his triumph at Wimbledon.

The Italian’s 94 percent win record in 2026 was the best of his career.

In his absence, Alexander Zverev has taken over as world number one.

“Over the past few months, together with my team, we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery,” the five-time major winner said in announcing the operation on Tuesday.

“After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.”

Spanish star Carlos Alcaraz , who, with Sinner, has become the pre-eminent force in men’s tennis, wished him well.

“Tennis misses him. I miss him,” the world number three, who has had his own injury battles, said on social media.

Sinner won his first Grand Slam in 2024 by beating Daniil Medvedev in five sets at Melbourne Park, then retained his title a year later with victory over Zverev.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open after knee surgery
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner is ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee.
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee.

The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July.

In a social media post on Tuesday, world number two Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee.

"We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO [Australian Open] in January following his recent surgery," said Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo.

"Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon."

The 2027 Australian Open main draw starts on 17 January.

Sinner's challenge at the 2026 tournament was ended by a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic.

Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches.

He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way.

However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title.

Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece.

He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025.

Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking.

Analysis, BBC tennis correspondent Russell Fuller

There was never any prospect of Sinner competing in the Australian Open once news of his operation was announced on Tuesday.

The recovery period will be months, rather than weeks, and in any case the preparation to play in Melbourne in temperatures in the 30C+ cannot be compromised.

Sinner's domination of the first half of the year means he will very likely remain in the world's top three until March - which is remarkable, given he will have been out for seven months by then.

His target will now be to get himself in prime condition to contest the three Grand Slams which take place between May and September.

But as with many operations undertaken by elite athletes, there is no guarantee the procedure will solve the problem for good.

Sinner will be desperate for a healthy body, as experience suggests the rest will then look after itself.

articles.title: Alcaraz añade el pie hacia arriba de Pete Sampras para mejorar su saque: "Buscábamos más balance"
articles.standfirst: El tenista ha moldeado su técnica y los resultados se han visto en la gira de superficie dura bajo techo
articles.summary: El tenista ha moldeado su técnica y los resultados se han visto en la gira de superficie dura bajo techo
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha llegado a la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis de Bolonia invicto esta temporada en superficie dura bajo techo, las condiciones del Super Tennis Arena de la capital de la región Emilia-Romaña. El triunfo ante Alexander Zverev en la final del Masters masculino era el decimoquinto a cubierto. Gran parte del éxito del fenómeno de El Palmar en ese hábitat hay que encontrarlo en la mejora del servicio desde el US Open. En el último grande del curso, Carlitos cedió en los cuartos con Ben Shelton en el súper tie break del quinto set. Cometió siete dobles faltas, sólo ganó el 69 por ciento de puntos con el primer saque y 51 con el segundo y encajó cinco roturas. “Quien pegue más fuerte a las líneas es el que gana. Cuanto más ajustado pegues los golpes, más porcentaje tienes de tener una posición de ataque o incluso ganar el punto. No suelo mirar las estadísticas en los entrenamientos. Sí que es verdad que las miro cuando salgo de los partidos porque es importante para la siguiente ronda. Sabemos de la importancia que tiene el saque. Es algo que hemos mejorado y le hemos puesto mucho hincapié. Desde el US Open es la vez que más empeño le he puesto en el servicio. Y la precisión era algo importante y lo hemos trabajado más porque no tengo mucha altura y no puedo sacar como otros jugadores”, se sincera. Alcaraz, que se le comparaba con Novak Djokovic en la puesta en escena de la bola a principios de enero cuando acudió al Open de Australia, ha añadido una variación técnica que le asemeja ahora a Pete Sampras. El estadounidense se hizo prácticamente inexpugnable al servicio gracias a lograr más balance, ritmo e impulso hacia arriba gracias a levantar el pie izquierdo en el momento de iniciar el movimiento. “Buscábamos que tuviera más balance en el inicio del movimiento y que eso le ayudara a estar más fluido y que pudiera impulsarse hacia arriba”, cuenta su entrenador Samuel López a MARCA. El objetivo era golpear la pelota lo más alto posible. Cuando a Carlitos le hablaron de su mejora al servicio en las ATP Finals, tuvo clara su respuesta: "Samu es un crack". El campeón de siete grandes es el segundo tenista que más partidos ha decantado a su favor este curso en superficie dura, con un total de 42. Sólo Daniil Medvedev (43) sumó más triunfos de momento. Y es que al murciano le restan la Copa Davis para seguir aumentando esas cifras. No lo podrá hacer este jueves, en los cuartos con Austria, porque el plan es que tenga descanso en los individuales y sólo dispute un hipotético dobles con Marcel Granollers en caso de que sea necesario y la serie vaya empate a uno. David Ferrer tiene plena confianza en Dani Mérida y Rafa Jódar, que saltarán a disputar los dos primeros puntos ante Lukas Neumayer y Jurij Rodionov. Carlitos realizó la mañana del miércoles el primer entrenamiento en Bolonia desde que el pasado domingo se coronó maestro en Turín. Se juntó con Granollers durante casi dos horas con la supervisión de Marc López, el segundo de Ferrer y al que relevará en la capitanía tras las presentes finales de Bolonia. “No han pasado muchos días, no tuve mucho descanso. He tocado la bola en el entreno, no ha sido lo exigente que suele ser un entrenamiento previo a empezar la competición. Tengo confianza plena en el equipo, juegue quien juegue”, dice. Carlitos se pone al servicio de la 'Armada'.

articles.title: AITA presidential election: Chintan Parekh vs Rohit Rajpal - two visions for Indian tennis
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The race for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) presidency pits Chintan Parekh's \"Tennis First\" motto against Rohit Rajpal's \"The Next
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The race for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) presidency pits Chintan Parekh's "Tennis First" motto against Rohit Rajpal's "The Next Serve," with both candidates promising to address Indian tennis' structural challenges.While Parekh's pitch centres on governance reform, financial sustainability and expanding tennis beyond established centres; Rajpal has outlined a more programme-driven roadmap with specific proposals, timelines and targets. Their approaches differ on how to tackle key issues confronting Indian tennis.1. Grassroots developmentChintan Parekh wants to expand talent scouting beyond established centres, with a focus on underserved regions such as the North-East. His vision includes coaching pyramids and grooming young players for a stronger tennis ecosystem by 2030.Rohit Rajpal proposes a state-wise development audit within 100 days, common talent-identification protocols, zonal camps, a central player database and low-cost talent scouting in underserved districts.2. Infrastructure developmentChintan Parekh wants to take tennis to regions lacking infrastructure, particularly beyond metropolitan centres, and tap talent in remote and underserved areas.Rohit Rajpal plans to expand national and zonal centres of excellence, partner state associations, develop infrastructure in the Northeast and hill regions, and explore a high-altitude training centre.3. More tournaments at domestic and international levelChintan Parekh focuses on strengthening AITA's finances to fund tennis development, but has not outlined specific targets for tournament expansion.Rohit Rajpal wants to bring ATP and WTA events back to India, expand Challenger, ITF and junior tournaments, rotate events across zones, and build women's and senior circuits with at least 30 tournaments annually by 2030.4. GovernanceChintan Parekh identifies better governance as the key pillar under his presidency. He promises transparent, player-centric governance and a clean-up of AITA's institutional structure. He wants the AITA Trust to be brought under the association's umbrella, its trustees restructured, and issues concerning AITA's relationship with Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA) resolved.Rohit Rajpal proposes published accounts, budgets and fund utilisation, along with Athletes, Ethics and Dispute Resolution committees. He also promises transparent selection criteria, calendars and measurable progress reports.5. How to make tennis financially viableChintan Parekh wants to build AITA's corpus to ₹200-250 crore over four years, tap CSR funding and create greater financial capacity to support budding players."Our vision is a very clean AITA with a focus on the players. Grassroots development is important so scholarships for talented children in rural areas(is one target).Tennis is still considered an affluent sport, one for the elite. The first step is to clean it up (the corruption). The second step is to build the grassroots, then get the funding in, empower the state associations who empower the players," Leander Paes, who is the vice-presidential candidate in Parekh's team, had told select media after filing his nomination.Rohit Rajpal proposes travel and tournament-entry assistance for professionals, a CSR-funded Players' Distress Fund and a feasibility study for a pension scheme for retired players.BOTTOM LINE: Two visions, one challengeParekh's pitch is centred on institutional reform, financial strength and widening tennis' reach. Rajpal's manifesto offers a structured roadmap with programmes, timelines and measurable targets.Both promise to address Indian tennis' longstanding challenges. The real test, however, will be turning those promises into tangible opportunities for players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev reacts after winning crucial Davis Cup match against Arthur Fery
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has just helped claim a crucial point for Germany in their Davis Cup Finals tie with Great Britain. Playing in the second match...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev has just helped claim a crucial point for Germany in their Davis Cup Finals tie with Great Britain.

Playing in the second match of the quarterfinal clash in Bologna, Zverev beat Arthur Fery 6-3, 6-2 after one hour and 10 minutes. The much-needed win arrived after Cameron Norrie beat Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3, 3-6, 6-2 to give Great Britain a 1-0 lead. ATP number one Zverev has since reacted to his victory over Fery, which leaves the tie evenly poised at 1-1 ahead of the doubles finale.

Alexander Zverev happy with crucial Davis Cup win vs Arthur Fery

Speaking on court right after the match, Zverev was asked how proud he was to deliver when his team needed him and to come out on top in his first Davis Cup match as world number one. He responded: "It's not something I think about, but I think yeah, the team needed me today. Of course we needed the win.

"And it's going to be a team effort winning here. So I'm happy that I could deliver today, but we're not through yet. We've got a very tough deciding doubles to play, and hopefully we can manage to win that as well."

And discussing how crucial his hold at 4-2 in the second set was, Zverev said: "Yeah, of course. It's nice to keep the break and be up in the match, and win the set 6-2 instead of being 4-3 and then you have to battle again. But yeah I'm very happy with the performance in general. I think first match here is never easy, but yeah I'm definitely happy right now."

The German was finally tasked with looking ahead to the crucial doubles tie, of which he said: "Yeah, two of the best teams in the world. I think the British is a new partnership for next year. Maybe we can spoil the mood a little bit for next year already."

Henry Patten and Neal Skupski are taking on Germans Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz, with the British duo playing their first match together as regular doubles partners. That arrives after Patten split with his partner Harri Heliovaara just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy.

articles.title: Davis Cup - Great Britain 2-1 Germany: Cameron Norrie guides side to first semi-finals appearance in seven years
articles.summary: Great Britain reach Davis Cup semis with 2-1 win over Germany; Cameron Norrie beats Jan-Lennard Struff before Alexander Zverev levels against Arthur Fery; Neal Skupski and Henry Patten win deciding doubles to book semi-final clash with Spain, who beat Austria in final quarter-final
articles.body:
Neal Skupski and Henry Patten outlasted Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz in a nail-biting second-set tie-break to seal a 6-2, 7-6(8-6) win and end Great Britain's seven-year wait for a Davis Cup semi-final appearance.

It came after world No 1 Alexander Zverev had drawn the tie level at 1-1 with a comfortable 6-3 6-2 win over Arthur Fery.

Earlier in the day, Cameron Norrie got Great Britain off to a fast start, besting Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3 3-6 6-2.

Great Britain will now play Spain on Saturday, after they defeated Austria on Thursday in the last quarter-final.

Spain secured their place with a 2-0 victory, thanks to singles wins for Daniel Merida, who beat Joel Schwaerzler 6-4 6-4 and Rafael Jodar, who fought back from a set down to defeat Jurij Rodionov 2-6 6-0 6-1.

Three-time defending champions Italy face Czech Republic in the other semi-final.

After sweeping Krawietz and Puetz away in the first set, the German duo hit back in the following exchange, forcing the Brits to a tie-break.

With a spot in the semi-final on the line, Krawietz and Puetz pushed their opponents to 5-5 in the decider, before Skupski produced the most incredible reaching backhand at the net, to keep his side ahead by a point.

Germany hit back and won the next point, but Britain were too strong, with Skupski sending Britain through to the semi-finals with a booming cross-court return.

"They are a very experienced team," Patten said.

"They've been playing together a lot longer than us. That's maybe an advantage; maybe they don't know what to expect from me and Neal, but they are a world-class outfit and they have had success for many, many years and lots of success in the Davis Cup as well.

"Helps having a guy on your team that can hit a return like that on match point."

Norrie cruised through the first set after breaking Struff at 3-1.

But Struff hit back, winning a break to go 3-5 in the next exchange to capitalise on a few poor errors from the Brit.

However, Norrie bounced back in the final set, emphatically saving four break points at 3-2, before breaking Struff twice late on to wrap up a big victory.

In a repeat of this year's Wimbledon singles semi-final, Zverev once again showed why he has risen to the world No 1 standings, comfortably and patiently dispatching Fery in an hour and 11 minutes.

Fery fought hard in the first set to keep level with the German, but Zverev was too powerful, pinning Fery deep into his court in the first set to break the 24-year-old at 2-2.

Another break followed to seal the first set, with Zverev swiping a booming winner across the court.

Fery has never beaten Zverev, nor has he won a set off the world No 1 in their three meetings.

The second set continued in a similar vein, with Zverev breaking Fery twice to keep his side in the clash.

By winning, Zverev also achieved a significant milestone, joining an exclusive group of players to record 70 tour-level wins in one calendar year. Only 12 other players have done so, with Roger Federer having done it six times.

"The team needed me today," Zverev said to the BBC . "Of course we needed the win. I'm happy that I could deliver today."
