articles.title: Can tennis hold its TV audience without Jannik Sinner? A 10 million Italian viewer drop at this year’s ATP Finals raises star-power concerns
articles.summary: The absence of Jannik Sinner at the ATP Finals leads to a staggering 10 million drop in Italian viewership, sparking discussions about tennis's reliance on star power to attract audiences.
articles.body: Tennis had a useful reminder this season that a strong field does not always guarantee a television audience. Jannik Sinner’s absence from the ATP Finals in Turin coincided with a substantial fall in Italian viewership, despite the presence of another home favourite, Flavio Cobolli, and a tournament eventually won by Carlos Alcaraz. The figures have reignited debate over tennis’s growing dependence on its biggest stars to attract television audiences.ATP Finals viewership takes a hit without SinnerSinner’s absence was particularly noticeable in Turin, where the Italian had won the ATP Finals in each of the previous two years and was chasing a third consecutive title on home soil. An injury prevented him from defending his crown after he confirmed in October that he would bring his 2026 season to an early end.The impact was reflected in Italian television figures. According to journalist Jose Moron of Punto de Break, the 2026 ATP Finals attracted approximately 10 million fewer viewers in Italy than the previous edition.The contrast was especially pronounced during the tournament’s decisive stages. In 2025, Sinner defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the final, producing one of the biggest audiences in Italian tennis broadcasting history. This time, Alcaraz overcame Alexander Zverev to claim his first ATP Finals title, but the tournament struggled to generate comparable interest among Italian viewers.Moron reported that one Italian broadcaster saw its audience share for the Alcaraz-Zverev match fall from nearly 30 per cent in 2025 to just 9 per cent in 2026. The figures were different in Spain, where Movistar recorded a slight increase, from three per cent to 3.1 per cent, across the two editions.Moron argued that Spain would likely have experienced a similar decline had Alcaraz been absent, suggesting that national loyalty plays a significant role in tennis viewership, with audiences particularly drawn to their own leading players.“The conclusion is that some people like tennis, but more people like Alcaraz or Sinner than tennis itself,” he said.The presence of Cobolli, who finished the season as world No 7 and earned a place in the eight-man field, did little to offset the loss of Sinner. The Italian failed to progress beyond the group stage, but his participation had offered another reason for the home crowd to follow the tournament.Sinner and Alcaraz bring audiences that tennis struggles to replaceThe previous year's final demonstrated just how powerful the Sinner-Alcaraz rivalry has become commercially. Their 2025 meeting broke Italian television records, with 6.7 million viewers watching Sinner defeat the Spaniard to win the ATP Finals.According to the ATP, the 2025 final became the most-watched tennis broadcast in Italian history, attracting 100,000 more viewers than Sinner’s victory over Novak Djokovic at Wimbledon in July 2025. The figures offered another indication of the audience drawn by the Italian, particularly when he faces Alcaraz, with their rivalry becoming one of the sport’s biggest attractions.The pattern was not confined to Italy this season. In the United States, the French Open final between Cobolli and Zverev averaged just 1.3 million viewers, making it the least-watched men's or women's singles final at a Grand Slam in 20 years, according to the reported figures. That represented a 25 per cent decline from the 2025 final, when Sinner and Alcaraz produced a memorable contest.The contrast was particularly striking because the 2026 Australian Open final, contested by Alcaraz and Djokovic, attracted a comparable American audience to the celebrated 2017 final between Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal.The figures suggest that the presence of recognisable names and established rivalries can make a considerable difference to the television appeal of major tournaments. A compelling match remains important, but the players involved often determine whether a casual audience decides to watch in the first place.Sinner and Djokovic have also been among the players raising concerns about the financial distribution of tennis revenues, prompting the ATP to announce a $500 million compensation plan aimed at addressing complaints about financial fairness. Their influence extends beyond the results on court, with the sport's leading names playing an increasingly important role in its commercial appeal.Italian tennis feels the absence of its biggest starThe decline in domestic viewing figures has also prompted a response from Italian Tennis Federation president Angelo Binaghi, who admitted that Sinner's influence had been greater than he anticipated.Speaking to Italian media, Binaghi recalled meeting the player at the Inalpi Arena in Turin and discussing the effect of his absence.“When I saw Sinner on Sunday at the Inalpi Arena, I confessed that he really surprised me, because I had no idea how dependent we were on him,” he said.“Every week, for decades, I’ve analyzed all the data on our tennis. But his absence has been felt much more than expected; just check the ratings: without him, they’re less than half.”Italy is hardly short of established players. Cobolli has enjoyed a breakthrough season, while Matteo Berrettini, Matteo Arnaldi, Luciano Darderi and Lorenzo Musetti have all contributed to the country's strong presence in men's tennis. Yet Binaghi believes none has the same ability to attract a broad audience as Sinner.“The other Italians are among the best in the world: some like Cobolli because he’s a fighter, aesthetes are in love with [Lorenzo] Musetti, for many Berrettini remains an idol.“But Jannik engages everyone, including those Italians who until three or four years ago knew little about tennis. Is he popular because he wins like Rossi or Tomba? Not only that.“It’s that he’s a popular character: the good red-haired boy from the mountains, a simple and clean family behind him, the sacrifices he’s made, the sportsmanship with which he presents himself. A narrative that clearly captures the attention.”Cobolli has also spoken about the pressure of being Italy's leading representative at the year-end tournament in Sinner's absence. His early exit meant the home crowd lost another reason to remain invested in the competition, although the viewing figures suggest the absence of the country's biggest star was the more significant factor.Sinner's return remains uncertain. The Australian Open has been mentioned as a possible target, but reports have questioned whether he will be ready, with some suggesting his recovery could extend beyond the 2027 tournament. Former world No 1 Mats Wilander has also suggested that the injury could keep the Italian out for about a year.Until a return date is confirmed, tennis will have to contend with the same problem exposed by the figures in Turin: even with a competitive field and a Grand Slam champion on court, replacing the audience drawn by Sinner is proving difficult.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Davis Cup Finals 2026: Great Britain beat Germany to reach semi-finals
articles.summary: Great Britain advance to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski win a decisive doubles tie against Germany in Bologna.
articles.body:
Great Britain advanced to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won a decisive doubles tie against third seeds Germany in Bologna.

Patten and Skupski, playing together for the first time since announcing their doubles partnership for the 2027 season, proved too clinical for Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.

They converted two break points and saved five in the first set, before overturning a mini-break in the tie-break to win 6-2 7-6 (8-6).

Skupski was involved in a Davis Cup quarter-final loss playing alongside Joe Salisbury against the same German doubles pair in December 2021 - a defeat that was in his mind as Thursday's decider progressed.

"I thought about that match during the match today and I was determined not to let that happen again," Skupski told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"No matter what was happening today, we weren't going to come off the court very easily with a loss."

World number one Alexander Zverev had earlier sent the tie to its full distance by defeating British number one Arthur Fery in straight sets to cancel out Cameron Norrie's three-set victory over Jan-Lennard Struff.

Great Britain's semi-final is scheduled for Saturday, when they will face Spain.

Spaniards Daniel Merida and Rafael Jodar won their singles matches, meaning the team did not need to play doubles, allowing Carlos Alcaraz to rest.

Captain David Ferrer said Alcaraz may be in contention to play in the singles against Great Britain.

Defending champions Italy will play the Czech Republic in Friday's first semi-final.

Recap: GB's Davis Cup quarter-final win against Germany as it happened

Smith will step down as captain at the end of the tournament and Great Britain retain hopes of a second victory under his leadership, following the most recent of their 10 Davis Cup successes in 2015.

"I felt the same sort of pressure, nerves and butterflies beforehand and during the matches," said Smith, who has been captain since 2010.

"You sit for a long time in that chair on your own on a day like this, a lot of thoughts go through your head and one of the things I kept reminding myself is how much of a privilege it is to be in this situation.

"I loved it but, more importantly, I'm thrilled for the guys. They've committed so well to this, they've been to a few different places over the past 18 months to get to this opportunity and I'm delighted they've got to the final four now."

World number 52 Norrie had got Great Britain off to the perfect start with a three-set win against Struff, a player 13 places above him in the world rankings.

The left-hander raced through the first set in just 23 minutes but a break late in the second set by Struff forced a decider.

The key moment came at 2-2 in the final set when Norrie saved four break points to hold serve, after which he won 12 of the next 14 points to complete a 6-3 3-6 6-2 victory.

Norrie's success meant a win for Fery against Zverev, a two-time major champion in 2026, would have been enough to secure Great Britain's passage through to the last four.

However, as he did in their Wimbledon semi-final in July, Zverev proved too strong for 24-year-old Fery and ended as a 6-3 6-2 winner.

Patten and Skupski have found themselves unusually in the spotlight over the past week following the former's "ruthless" split from Harri Heliovaara in favour of joining forces with his compatriot next season.

While their partnership is in its infancy, there were few signs of teething problems as they extended their Davis Cup record as a pair to 3-0.

Patten's pinpoint returns and sharp reactions at the net coupled with Skupski's impressive serving proved too strong for Krawietz and Puetz, who were left to rue missed opportunities.

In a sticky opening service game, Patten double-faulted on the opening point and faced a break point, while Skupski saved four in game seven of the opening set.

Neither pair earned a break point in the second set, with the British duo dropping just five points on serve.

Trailing 3-1 in what turned out to be a thrilling tie-break, they fought back to lead 6-5 before closing out the win at the second opportunity.

"It doesn't feel like the end of the season for those two because they've just paired up," Smith said. "There's been a buoyancy in their practice sessions because it's a new start.

"They were brilliant today. You don't know if you're going to get a match or not [as doubles players] but I saw them 20 minutes before their match and you could just see they were delighted to get this opportunity and that gave them a huge lift."

articles.title: Jurij Rodionov - Rafa Jódar resumen, estadísticas y resultado de los cuartos de final de la Copa Davis
articles.summary: Lo dejamos por aquí hoy. Disponible la crónica del partido en MARCA. Seguro que seguiremos teniendo grandes noticias del equipo español en el futuro.
articles.body:
Buenas tardes, bienvenidos a los cuartos de final de la Copa Davis. Hoy tendremos en la pista central del Super Tennis Arena de Bolonia a la Selección Española, que se estrena en esta 'Final a 8' ante Austria. Hay que recordar que primero se disputan los dos encuentros individuales, y si hay empate, el dobles decidirá el tercer punto. Rafa Jódar y Jurij Rodionov serán los encargados de disputar el duelo por el segundo punto de la eliminatoria.

Tras 81 partidos a sus espaldas, Rafa Jódar aterriza en Bolonia para disputar su primera 'Final a 8' de Copa Davis. Debutó a lo grande en la clasificatoria en tierras chilenas, endosándole a Garín un 6-0 y 6-2, y hoy tiene la oportunidad de convertir a los de David Ferrer en equipo de semifinales. Para ello, primero tendrá que derrotar al austriaco Rodionov, actual número 119 del ranking ATP.

En la eliminatoria de hoy, el madrileño tiene la condición de primer espada en los individuales ya que Carlos Alcaraz solo saltará a pista si hay necesidad de jugar el dobles definitivo.

articles.title: Jódar se sobrepone ante Rodionov y da el billete a las semifinales de la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: El joven de Leganés ejerce de número 1, remonta un set y certifica la semifinal contra Gran Bretaña
articles.summary: El joven de Leganés ejerce de número 1, remonta un set y certifica la semifinal contra Gran Bretaña
articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha clasificado este jueves a España por segundo año consecutivo para las semifinales de la Copa Davis tras remontar a Jurij Rodionov, para cerrar un tanteo de 2-6, 6-0 y 6-1. El tenista del Club de Tenis Chamartín ha nacido para grandes momentos y los mejores escenarios. Y el Super Tennis Arena de Bolonia es uno de ellos. Respondió a la presión de haber cedido un set, con un contundente rosco. De hecho, sólo perdió un juego más. Tiene el temple de los elegidos. La selección nacional de la Copa Davis cumplió el test inicial de Austria y ya piensa en el mañana, que será la semifinal con Gran Bretaña, el único equipo que ha participado en todas las ediciones del torneo desde 1900. La primera consecuencia de la presencia del equipo británico en el camino de España es que no habrá este sábado una repetición de la final de las ATP Finals de Turín entre Carlos Alcaraz y Alexander Zverev. El murciano cambia al número 1 por Arthur Fery, el 32 de las listas gracias a las semifinales en el último Wimbledon. El quinteto español es presente y futuro. Dani Mérida, 22 años, y Jódar, 20, dieron los dos primeros puntos, como ya habían hecho antes en los playoff clasificatorios de Chile en septiembre. Junto a Alcaraz son la base de una formación que es favorita para levantar la Ensaladera de plata en 2026 y en el futuro inmediato. Ninguna formación tiene jugadores tan jóvenes y con tanto talento como la Armada nacional. Fuera de la convocatoria se ha quedado Martín Landaluce, que a sus 20 primaveras será la representación española en las Next Gen Finals de Reggio Calabria como primer cabeza de serie. El jugador con más nombre de los austriacos es su capitán Jürgen Melzer. Este buscó la sorpresa situando en pista al díscolo Joel Schwaerzler, campeón júnior de Roland Garros en dobles, en 2024. Mérida le cerró muy rápido la puerta, con un doble 6-4, y dio tranquilidad a Jódar para firmar la sentencia a pesar de la losa que suponen para él sus 82 partidos jugados en la primera campaña como profesional. Rafa, una semana después de despedirse de la cita de maestros con derrota en la fase de grupos ante Ben Shelton, saboreó la victoria frente a Rodionov. Ya son 59 partidos ganados en el curso, el segundo que más de la élite sólo por detrás de Zverev (69). La victoria por la vía rápida de los elegidos por parte de David Ferrer permite a Alcaraz ganar dos días de descanso y recuperación para lo que viene y que es realmente lo importante. El flamante maestro ATP jugará, a partir de ahora, los individuales y podría estar también en el dobles, al lado de Marcel Granollers, en caso de que sea necesario y la serie vaya 1-1.

articles.title: David Ferrer se rinde a Mérida y Jódar: "Ha sido impresionante cómo han manejado la presión"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador nacional se congratula del rendimiento de Jódar y Mérida en sus primeras finales de la Copa Davis
articles.summary: El seleccionador nacional se congratula del rendimiento de Jódar y Mérida en sus primeras finales de la Copa Davis
articles.body: La selección nacional de la Copa Davis mostraba su satisfacción tras acceder por segundo año seguido a las semifinales de la máxima competición por países. David Ferrer decía que "estoy muy contento y muy orgulloso. Ha sido impresionante cómo han manejado la situación y la presión. Como capitán en la silla es muy bonito verles jugar. Vamos a ver si está listo Carlos para jugar el sábado". Rafa Jódar daba crédito al primer set de Jurij Rodionov: "En el segundo set, estuve muy sólido y el apoyo del banquillo me ha ayudado a ganar. Aquí todos te pueden ganar y yo no sentía la pelota en el primer set. Tener un ranking mejor no significa que vayas a ganar fácil. Estaba más relajado por la victoria de Dani. Si el capitán decide ponerme el sábado, intentaré darlo todo por España". Ferrer avisaba del potencial de Gran Bretaña: "Tienen el mejor dobles que hay aquí en Bolonia. Ahora toca descansar y disfrutar de la semifinal".

articles.title: Mirra Andreeva’s Grand Slam total for 2027 has already been predicted, ‘I would be surprised’
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva has set high expectations heading into the 2027 season. Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals titles this year, as well...
articles.body:
Mirra Andreeva has set high expectations heading into the 2027 season.

Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals titles this year, as well titles in Adelaide and Linz, in what has been the best season of her career so far.

These victories mean that Andreeva has a chance to become world number one by dethroning Elena Rybakina as early as the Australian Open next year.

With Andreeva becoming a Grand Slam champion for the first time this year, there is an expectation that the teenager will continue adding to her major tally in 2027.

Mirra Andreeva predicted to win one Grand Slam in 2027 by Steve Flink

Andreeva has reached the second week of all four Grand Slam tournaments, but Roland Garros is by far her best major tournament with an 85.7% win record, which she helped achieve this year after winning the title.

The Russian also matched her best result at the Australian Open this year, with Andreeva also going two rounds further than she had ever before at the US Open , where she had two match points in her quarter-final against Coco Gauff .

When discussing Andreeva's victory at the WTA Finals, Tennis Hall of Fame journalist Steve Flink admitted he was surprised at just how dominant she was at the year-end tournament. While Flink does not expect Andreeva to completely dominate the WTA Tour next year, he backed her to win another Grand Slam title in 2027 and have deep runs at all the majors.

"So Andreeva wins the event without losing a set," Flink said on Court-side with Beilinson Tennis . "That's awfully encouraging to her boosters for next year. To think, okay it wasn't the smoothest ride after Roland Garros. Although, she had a couple of match points against Coco at the US Open in the quarters that could have made a huge difference. It was frustrating losses like that were setting her back a bit.

"But boy does she end the year on a high note and I think it's going to carry into the Australian with a lot of confidence. I'm not suggesting that she's just going to suddenly take over women's tennis, it's not that simple. There's a lot of awfully good players at the top. But she's going to make her presence known.

"To back up winning Roland Garros by winning the year-end championships is a very impressive feat to me, especially to do it that convincingly on hard courts where all the players are so capable. It's not as if it's a dominant surface for her and she won her major on clay. So to do it on hard at the end of the year in Indian Wells, I must say I tip my hat to her and I will be watching her pretty closely, because she'll be coming into Melbourne and she'll be pretty tough to beat there based on what we saw here."

Flink added, "I'd add to that that I'd be surprised if we didn't see another major for her next year somewhere. Could it be more? Maybe. But more likely just one, but getting deep into all the rest. She'll contend and she can play against anybody in the upper levels of the sport right now. Nobody's going to dominate her.

"So it was not what I expected going into that tournament. If someone said to me well not only would she win the tournament, she won't drop a set, I would have said you're crazy. It's not that simple, it's not that easy against the top eight. Well, she made it easy and she won a bunch of love sets and was never even taken into a tie-break in this event."

Andreeva is now in her off-season, with just over a month until the 2027 season gets underway down under in Australia.
